subject: Mercury Health - Hosted API: data residency, retention & deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Sam Bennett <sam.bennett@mercuryhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency & deletion — hosted API questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team had a compact set of follow-ups focused on data residency, retention windows, and the practical steps for a customer-initiated erasure (GDPR/CCPA workflow). I pulled the top items below — can you confirm what Redwood supports for hosted API customers in the US?

1) Is customer data ever stored outside the US for hosted API calls? If yes — when/why and which regions?
2) What is the default retention for request/response logs (request bodies, request metadata, full responses)?
3) How does the deletion/erasure process work for a tenant: timeline, manual vs API-initiated, backups, and proof of deletion?
4) Are there any residual caches or KV stores that might retain PII beyond the stated retention?
5) For customers with PHI-like payloads, do you provide tailored retention / isolation options?

We'd like a short, plain-English reply we can include in our vendor risk assessment. If you need to loop others in, please do.

Best,
Sam
Sam Bennett
Director, InfoSec
Mercury Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data residency & deletion — hosted API questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping Neha (Security) and Rishi (Product Ops) for specifics. Below is a short summary; we'll follow up with a concise one-page statement and an attachment with timelines and the erasure runbook.

High-level answers (short):
- Residency: Hosted API requests for US customers are served from US regions by default. We do not replicate request/response payloads to non-US regions for standard hosted customers.
- Retention: Request metadata and operational logs: 30 days by default. Request/response payloads that hit logging (see below) are retained for 30 days unless a different contract option is selected.
- Deletion: Customers can request erasure via the Console or API. Standard erasure completes within 30 days; urgent erasures (compliance) can be expedited to 5 business days with a support ticket and audit.
- Caches/backups: Ephemeral KV caches are kept only in memory and evicted on session end; persistent backups are rotated with a 30-day retention and encrypted. We provide attestations for deletion from primary stores; deletion in backups follows the standard backup lifecycle (30 days) and is not immediate.
- PHI/regulated payloads: We have Dedicated and Private options for isolation and can apply custom retention/TTL configs for hosted enterprise customers under contract.

We'll send the written statement and the erasure playbook in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Mercury questions — need specific phrasing for vendor assessment

Mina / Rishi — drafting suggested vendor-assessment wording. A few technical clarifications I need before Mina replies to Sam: 

A) "Request metadata" definition: does this include headers and IP addresses for hosted API? We log source IPs for rate limit / abuse detection — retention consistent with other logs?
B) Backups: are nightly incremental backups retained beyond 30 days for disaster recovery? If so, what's the max snapshot TTL?
C) Ephemeral caches: confirm that KV cache contents are not persisted to disk under normal operation (only in-memory).

Suggested short paragraph for Mercury (we can adapt):
"Redwood's Hosted API processes requests in US-based regions for US customers. Operational logs and request metadata (including service-level headers and source IPs used for security and rate-limiting) are retained by default for 30 days. If a customer requires a shorter retention window, we can offer a contractual configuration for 7/14/30 day options. Customer-initiated erasure requests submitted via API or Console are executed against primary and indexed storage within 30 days; expedited deletions are available on request and include an audit statement. Backups are retained for a standard 30-day window and are deleted according to our backup lifecycle; restoration copies may exist within that window. Ephemeral KV caches are in-memory only and evicted routinely; they are not persisted to disk in standard hosted deployments."

Rishi — can you confirm (A-C) and sign off on phrasing?

Neha
Principal, Security
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Mercury questions — need specific phrasing for vendor assessment

Neha / Mina — confirmed and minor edits below. My answers: 
A) Yes — request metadata includes service headers and source IPs. We redact caller IPs from analytic exports by default but keep them in access logs for 30 days (security/forensics).
B) Backups: Nightly snapshots are kept up to 30 days. There are also weekly long-term snapshots stored for 90 days for disaster recovery across the cluster (this is not customer-visible and applies to our infra recovery only). We should disclose the 30-day customer-facing backup retention and avoid calling out the 90-day internal recovery snapshots in a vendor assessment unless asked.
C) KV caches: Confirmed in-memory only; we do not flush caches to disk in normal operation.

Edits to the suggested paragraph (keeps it customer-focused):
"Redwood's Hosted API processes requests in US-based regions for US customers. Operational logs and request metadata (including service-level headers and source IPs used for security and rate-limiting) are retained by default for 30 days; we can offer contractually scoped retention windows of 7, 14, or 30 days. Customer-initiated erasure requests submitted via the Console or API are executed against primary and indexed storage within 30 days; expedited erasures (5 business days) are available for regulated requests and include a deletion attestation. Backups used for customer restoration are retained on a 30-day schedule. Ephemeral KV caches remain in-memory only and are evicted routinely; they are not persisted to disk under standard hosted operation."

Mina — feel free to send this to Sam. I'll attach the erasure runbook and the deletion attestation template.

Rishi
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference
